title: Cream of Tomato Soup
subtitle: smooth, bright, and deeply satisfying
excerpt: This soup uses tinned tomatoes for a consistent result all year round. The cream smooths out the acidity and gives a silky finish. It comes together in under 40 minutes and tastes far better than anything from a tin.
sourceNotes: A British staple since the mid-20th century, adapted from earlier French pureed tomato soups. Commonly made with tinned tomatoes in home kitchens.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the cream. Stir in cream after reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe easily. Blends well in large batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Reheat gently and stir in cream just before serving.

content.text: If you have a stick blender, use it directly in the pan. If using a jug blender, let the soup cool slightly first and do not fill it more than halfway -- hot liquid expands.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and carrot. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the bay leaves. Add the basil leaves. Blend until very smooth.
Pass through a sieve if you want a very silky result. Stir in the cream.
Season with salt and pepper. Reheat gently and serve with crusty bread.

items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar or a splash more cream to balance.
Add a splash of hot water or extra stock and blend again.

items.cause: Not blended long enough or not sieved
items.fix: Blend for longer and pass through a fine sieve.

content.text: Cream of tomato soup became a British household staple after the tinned version was introduced in the early 20th century. The home-cooked version uses the same convenience of tinned tomatoes but with a far richer result. Fresh basil is a nod to the Italian origins of tomato cookery. This is the soup most British people grew up eating, now made from scratch.
